issues.legal_issue: The ordinary filing period for a revision before the revisional authority is guidance rather than a strict limitation period, and a revision is not barred merely because an affected party was added after that period.
material_facts: The revision was filed within sixty days of the order sought to be revised.
The affected allottees were added as parties after the sixty-day period had expired, and no application to excuse delay in adding them was made.
The revisional authority added them because its decision could prejudice their interests and gave them a reasonable opportunity to be heard.
The Court found no perversity or unreasonableness in the authority entertaining the revision.
issues.conclusion: The revision was not barred by time.
issues.legal_principle: Section 27 of the Administration of Evacuee Property Act, 1950 gives the Custodian-General revisional power exercisable at any time. Rule 31(5) of the Administration of Evacuee Property (Central) Rules, 1950, which says a revision should ordinarily be made within sixty days, is a rule of guidance and not a limitation period. The authority must exercise its judicial discretion reasonably. Section 5 of the Limitation Act does not apply because no period of limitation is prescribed for such a revision.

rule.if: custodian_general_revision and revision_filed_within_ordinary_period and affected_person_added_later and affected_person_given_hearing and authority_acted_reasonably

predicates.custodian_general_revision: The proceeding is a revision before the highest administrative revisional authority of this kind.
predicates.revision_filed_within_ordinary_period: The revision was filed within the period ordinarily expected for such filings.
predicates.affected_person_added_later: A person whose interests could be affected was made a party after that ordinary period had passed.
predicates.affected_person_given_hearing: The authority gave the later-added person a reasonable opportunity to be heard.
predicates.authority_acted_reasonably: The authority exercised its discretion to entertain the revision reasonably.

issues.definition: When a revision is filed within the ordinary period and a later-added affected person is heard, a reasonable decision to entertain the proceeding means it is not barred merely because that person was added later.

issues.legal_issue: The revisional authority may cancel an allotment made by a lower authority before the applicable cutoff when it does so in a revision it is entitled to entertain.
material_facts: The allotments at issue were made by a lower authority before the cutoff specified in the applicable rule.
The Custodian-General cancelled part of the allotment in deciding the displaced person's revision.
The revision was entertained within the period the Custodian-General considered appropriate in the exercise of discretion under the applicable rule.
issues.conclusion: The Custodian-General had power to cancel the allotment.
issues.legal_principle: Section 27 of the Administration of Evacuee Property Act, 1950 authorises the Custodian-General to revise an order of a Custodian and make an appropriate order. Although rule 14(6) of the Administration of Evacuee Property (Central) Rules, 1950 restricts a Custodian's power to cancel certain rural allotments, its second proviso permits the Custodian-General, in a revision under section 27, to cancel an allotment made by a lower authority before the specified cutoff. Read with rule 31(5), the prescribed period for such a revision is ordinarily sixty days, but the Custodian-General may in discretion entertain it later.

predicates.custodian_general_revision: The proceeding is a revision before the highest administrative revisional authority of this kind.
predicates.lower_authority_allotment_before_cutoff: The allotment being challenged was made by a lower authority before the applicable cutoff.
predicates.revision_entertained_within_discretionar: The authority entertained the revision within the ordinary period or within a later period it reasonably accepted in its discretion.

issues.definition: When the proceeding is a revision of a pre-cutoff allotment made by a lower authority and the revision is entertained within the authority's permissible period, the authority may cancel the allotment.

issues.legal_issue: An allotment may be treated as existing where the record contains no clear finding that it did not exist and its existence was not disputed during the proceedings.
material_facts: The challenged order referred to an allotment in favour of the affected group, while noting that supporting claim records could not be found or produced.
The observations in the order did not clearly find that no allotment had been made.
The fact that the group had been allotted the land was not questioned throughout the proceedings.
issues.conclusion: The appeal was decided on the basis that an allotment in favour of the group existed, and the contention that there was no allotment was rejected.
issues.legal_principle: The Court distinguished observations about missing supporting records from a clear finding that no allotment existed. Since the allotment itself had not been questioned during the proceedings, it proceeded on the basis that the allotment existed; it identified no separate statutory provision or earlier case as the basis for this conclusion.

predicates.allotment_existence_undisputed: The parties did not question during the proceedings whether the allotment had been made.
predicates.no_clear_finding_of_no_allotment: The decision under review did not clearly find that the allotment had never been made.

issues.definition: When the allotment's existence was not disputed and the record contains no clear finding that it did not exist, the allotment is treated as existing.
